redraws.to: ivory and charcoal with muted lilac
redraws.reason: Client decision: mature ivory/charcoal foundation with restrained lilac; crimson reads studio-aggressive and does not carry the refined, subtly feminine identity asked for.

A pure-grotesk monument is the category default for AI and engineering sites. A sharp display serif over the same General Sans text face keeps the monument but stops it reading as another generated tech portfolio, and adds the editorial, slightly feminine register without decoration.

redraws.from: ring of frames around the headline
redraws.reason: The ring needs 18-24 real project photographs. None exist. The skill forbids planning around pictures you do not have.
The scatter needs five to eight full-bleed project photographs. The ledger scales from three projects to twenty, needs one image per project, and is keyboard- and touch-operable.

ideaSentence: On this page, the gap between what a person has built and what an AI system believes about them becomes a measured column of accumulated margin - the page's one drawing, and the visual argument for the work it lists.

liveThing.name: the ledger rule
liveThing.what: The Selected Work section draws one glyph per shipped project in the page margin. It accumulates as the visitor scrolls and again as they open projects; hovering or focusing a ledger row pulls that project's mark into view.
liveThing.proves: That a context layer should be legible, bounded and inspectable rather than a black box - the claim ContextOS makes.
liveThing.phone: becomes a horizontal register at the top of Selected Work, left marks clearing as right marks fill
liveThing.fallback: without JS it is a static column of marks, each with its project name in a title element; the ledger list stays fully readable and every link still works

sections.heading: Selected Work

sections.desktop: ledger column 560px wide with its left edge at 22% of the viewport. Rows 44px tall: name 16px in full ink at the left; kind of work 16px in muted at 55% of the column; year right-aligned, tabular figures. No rules between rows. Hover or focus a row: that row stays full ink, the others drop to muted, and the project's image appears in the empty area right of the column - 4:3, 300px wide, absolutely positioned, top aligned to the hovered row, 64px from the column's right edge, 150ms fade.
sections.mobile: column full width with 20px margins; rows 52px tall with the name left and the year right, kind of work on a second line at 13px. No hover preview: the first three projects each show a 16:10 image at full column width above their row.

artisticElement.name: The ledger rule
artisticElement.concept: One mark per shipped project, drawn in the page margin, accumulating as the visitor scrolls and again as they open projects. Each mark is the project's own initial, rendered as a glyph from a small set of drawn skeletons - never a node graph, never a particle field, never a neural-network illustration.
artisticElement.reference: an accountant's tally and a seismograph trace - two traditions of recording, both legible, both bounded
artisticElement.construction: inline SVG, stroke-width 1.25, round caps, drawn from a fixed glyph table; two layers - a dim base layer always visible and a lilac overlay layer whose stroke-dashoffset is driven by scroll progress. No canvas, no animation loop, no particles.

behaviour.onScroll: each mark fills as its project's row passes; the column accumulates top to bottom
behaviour.onHoverOrFocus: that project's mark pulls out to 8px to the right and rises to full ink
behaviour.onOpen: one additional segment is appended to the open project's mark, permanently for the session
behaviour.reducedMotion: the base layer shows all marks at once with no travel and no dash animation

artisticElement.verification: built and inspected as a standalone file at 1440px: the SVG produced no hairline finding. The inspector only counts thin rules made from CSS borders, 1-1.5px background elements and gradients - stroked SVG paths are not counted. This was tested, not assumed.
artisticElement.placement: the right page margin beside Selected Work on desktop; a horizontal register above the Selected Work list on mobile

ledger.pointer: hover a row - row to full ink, siblings to muted, preview image fades in over 150ms
ledger.keyboard: rows are real links; focus produces the same state as hover; focus ring is 2px solid rose #C9A0A0 at 2px offset, visible on both ivory and charcoal
ledger.touch: no hover dependency: each project image is rendered inline above its row at phone width, so a tap on the row follows the link and the image is already visible
ledger.tapTarget: 44px minimum row height on desktop, 52px on phone

motion.signature: masked headline - each line rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms strong ease-out, line two 110ms after line one; the supporting sentence and the button fade up together
motion.sections: heading, then text, then picture or figure, staggered 60-90ms, rising 16-32px with opacity, triggered once as the section enters
motion.feedback: press, hover and focus on every button, link, ledger row and contact row
motion.movingPicture: one slow drift on the Selected Work preview image
motion.floor: the inspector fails a page under eight moving elements; budget for twelve to sixteen
motion.reducedMotion: every move keeps its content and drops its travel; nothing is hidden if the script fails

responsive.margins: 40px desktop, 32px tablet, 16px phone; equal on both sides at every width
rules: the phone layout is its own composition, not a squeeze of the desktop one
the ledger preview is a hover affordance on desktop only; on phone each project carries its image inline
the ledger rule becomes horizontal on phone
the monument name stays two lines at every width

the research row is a placeholder pending verified title, venue and date; no research claim may be published until confirmed
the inspector warns when a page carries no video; no honest clip exists yet, so the warning will be defended rather than filled
